text:
maya (support): Hey team — ACME (customer: jenna) hit a spike of streaming failures this morning. They report a bunch of requests showing client disconnect / broken pipe during chunked responses, but our gateway is marking them as 5xx. Sample request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d.

maya (support): Here's the snippet they pasted from their client: 
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" -H \"Transfer-Encoding: chunked\" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/streams/generate -d @payload.json
```
payload.json contains multiple small chunks sent slowly (heartbeat ~3s). They see intermittent `write(): broken pipe` on their side.

maya (support): Customer is worried they're being charged for 5xx tokens; they saw ~40 failed streams in last hour and billing flagged 5 of them as 5xx.

jenna (acme-customer): we only paused large uploads — this started after we added a simple heartbeat between chunks. before that everything was fine. we can reproduce reliably ~1/10 requests in staging.

raj (infra): Thanks — can you share request-ids? need gateway logs + proxy logs. maya, can you add the ids?

maya (support): Added a few: rq_0a1b2c3d, rq_0a1b2c4e, rq_0a1b2c5f. attaching the gateway trace (redacted) shows: 
```
[gateway] 2024-06-29T09:12:03Z rq_0a1b2c3d upstream write failed: write: broken pipe (EPIPE)\n
[gateway] 2024-06-29T09:12:03Z rq_0a1b2c3d classify: upstream_error -> 502\n
[proxy] 2024-06-29T09:12:03Z rq_0a1b2c3d connection FIN from client mid-chunk
```

lin (sre): So proxy sees client FIN mid-chunk, gateway maps to upstream write error and returns 502. That definitely looks like client-initiated abort, not an internal server error. We should not count these as 5xx for billing.

henry (support): We have an existing heuristic that if upstream write fails with EPIPE we classify as client-abort and mark 2xx? I thought that was the case, but logs show gateway still surfaces 502. Might be a regression in the error handling path introduced with the chunked-trailer support patch.

lin (sre): Repro plan: get a tcpdump from customer's staging run + gateway debug logs. Also run an internal reproducer that mimics slow-chunk heartbeat and force an immediate FIN from a client to see how our ingress layers behave. I can run that in the next 90m.

raj (infra): @lin please capture the exact kernel errno we see in the write path. If it's EPIPE/EHOSTUNREACH vs ECONNRESET, we may need a mapping change in the classification layer. Also check if the proxy (nginx/envoy) sends a 502 upstream or if we generate it ourselves.

maya (support): Jenna — can you enable verbose client logs for one failing session and share the pcap? If you can't, at minimum we need the X-Request-Id header value and a rough timeline.

jenna (acme-customer): pcap attached to the ticket INC-2024-455. we captured a FIN 120ms after the last chunk fragment. we did see a TCP RST on one run.

henry (support): Based on that timeline, it smells like an intermediary (customer side proxy or NAT) sending FIN during heartbeat. Two things to address: 1) customer troubleshooting (their network) and 2) platform side — don't bill as 5xx when client aborts pre-finish.

lin (sre): Quick check: current billing pipeline flags 5xx if final response status >=500 OR if gateway returned an upstream_error tag. We need to differentiate upstream_error caused by client-side close. Proposed change: surface a new transport-level reason (client_aborted_midstream) and exclude it from billing 5xx.

raj (infra): Agree. We'll also add a metric to count these separately for alerting. If it's due to a regression in chunked-trailer handling, we must roll back the change or patch.

maya (support): Action items: 
- lin: run reproducer + attach gateway debug logs (ETA 90m)
- raj: review error-classification codepath, see if chunked-trailer patch altered errno mapping (ETA 4h)
- henry: update INC-2024-455 with billing hold request and ask finance to pause auto-billing for affected invoices until classification confirmed
- jenna: provide one more pcap if possible and confirm client proxy config (ETA 2h)

deploy-bot: Rollout:chunked-trailer-fix v2 started -> deploy_2024_06_28_18:30 UTC (info).

lin (sre): During the reproducer I see this sequence: client sends chunk header, wait heartbeat, then client FIN. Kernel write returns -32 (EPIPE). Our worker catches this and currently transforms into 502 with upstream_error. We should instead map EPIPE -> client_aborted_midstream and return 499-like internal marker (not billable).

raj (infra): If we alter mapping we must ensure no real upstream bugs get misclassified. Add a guard: only map to client_aborted_midstream if proxy observed FIN/RST from client within X ms of last client chunk and if response body not marked complete. That reduces false-negatives.

henry (support): I'll draft a short support note to send ACME: explain likely client-side proxy terminating heartbeats, steps to capture pcap, and confirm we will hold billing on suspect traces while we investigate.

maya (support): For the ticket, I've added command to reproduce locally: 
```
# simple repro: chunked upload with heartbeat then close
python3 reproduce_chunked_abort.py --heartbeat 3 --force-close-after 1-in-10
# script will print X-Request-Id header to match against gateway logs
```

maya (support): Closing loop: once lin or raj confirm classification fix or config rule, we'll backfill and re-evaluate billing flags for last 24h for ACME account.

jenna (acme-customer): thanks — we'll stand by and send the extra pcap. appreciate the quick triage.

lin (sre): Update: repro confirmed locally, kernel errno EPIPE mapped to upstream_error in current release. I pushed a small change in a branch to remap to client_aborted_midstream and added testcases. I'll open PR and request review from raj.

raj (infra): Reviewing now. If tests pass we'll cut a hotfix and patch production. Also adding a new metric `stream.client_abort_midstream` and dashboard panels.

henry (support): Finance asked for the list of request-ids impacted so they can reconcile credits; pulling from logs now and attaching to INC-2024-455.

maya (support): Thanks everyone. I'll update ACME and leave ticket open until hotfix deployed and billing re-eval'd.

jenna (acme-customer): confirmed we unblocked a staging subnet on our side and the failure rate dropped to near zero. looks like a customer network appliance was closing idle connections. will still provide pcap for completeness.

maya (support): Great — marking this as actionable (INC-2024-455) and we'll follow up when patch goes live. :thumbsup:
